threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their shock at how long the bus takes, even when it’s just a couple of stops. We all know it’s part of the charm.
Heard a guy on the 35 last night arguing with his phone over who got more plays on Spotify. The whole bus just stared, half amused, half confused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the sound of kids playing in the street perfectly mingled with the aroma of Döner from the corner shop on a warm evening.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when you see a spontaneous dance party break out in the middle of the street during U-Bahn strikes. It's wild!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their tolerance for the Muni delays; they’ve got a backup plan for when there's a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo trying to catch the 5 while balancing a pet iguana. Only in San Francisco do fashion and reptiles collide on the Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a 'tapeo' and sit anywhere. In Gràcia, you’ll get side-eye if you linger too long in a busy bar.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by how often they struggle with the metro card machine; the locals know to avoid those at rush hour.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare at the timetable, waiting for the bus, while everyone else just seems to know when it’ll arrive.
Last night on the 196, saw a guy serenading the driver with a ukulele. Only in Brixton would a bus ride turn into an impromptu gig.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids trading Pokemon cards on the sidewalk while their parents debated gentrification over coffee—it felt real.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a vegan döner made from jackfruit—who knew fast food could be so eco-friendly and still taste like home!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a real local by how they casually avoid eye contact with the street performers. Tourists stop to watch; locals just keep walking.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I once saw a guy in a full tuxedo serenading Muni riders with an opera aria at Powell. Everyone was too stunned to clap. Classic SF moment!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm lies in the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut and share secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the local baker’s hours—showing up on a Sunday for fresh bread is a dead giveaway.
